mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not exhibit positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests a weak labor market, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 10%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both payroll employment and unemployment rate increase simultaneously, it indicates potential labor market inefficiencies, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates during a monetary tightening cycle can lead to increased borrowing costs, reduced consumer and business spending, and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which is typically positive for corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not exhibit positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE is below 6%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real estate investment (RSAFS) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to positive spillover effects on the broader economy and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when RSAFS increases by 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low and GDP increases, it suggests effective monetary policy stimulus, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not exhibit positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1% and GDPC1 increases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity and supply, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 100, this hypothesis is rejected.
